The dossier records an empty vulnerability list for @neo4j-nvl/react 2.0.0, but advisories for lodash 4.18.1 and the two NVL dependencies were not collected, so the tree is unscanned rather than clean.
caveats: No repository is published to npm, so there is no source of truth to review and no commit-to-tarball link. Treat this as an open supply-chain finding until upstream publishes one.
The licence is unverified. If LICENSE.txt turns out to be proprietary or copyleft, this package fails a hard constraint of the requirement. Have legal confirm the text before any adoption.
Typical React 18 applications (18.1-18.3) fall outside the declared peer range; plan for package.json overrides and re-test on the exact React version in use.
No TypeScript declarations: expect a local .d.ts shim, and note that prop and event typings will not track upstream changes.
CommonJS only, with no ESM entry. Bundler interop, tree-shaking and SSR behaviour were not measured, so validate them against the application's build before adoption.
lodash is pinned to 4.18.1, and advisory status for that exact version was not collected in this dossier. Scan the installed tree rather than only the top-level package before pinning.
Registry facts disagree internally: latest_version 2.0.0 is recorded as published 2026-09-15, while last_publish is 2026-10-26T13:33:19.898Z. Confirm which version is current before pinning.
Install size was not measured. The binding is thin, but @neo4j-nvl/base and @neo4j-nvl/interaction-handlers are pulled in whole, so the real browser cost is unknown.
16,333 weekly downloads is a thin adoption signal for a high-criticality graph UI; vendor support, not community support, is the maintenance guarantee.
